short_product_summary: Kisspeptin-10 is the ten-residue C-terminal fragment of kisspeptin-54, the peptide product of the human KISS1 gene. Its sequence is Tyr-Asn-Trp-Asn-Ser-Phe-Gly-Leu-Arg-Phe-NH2, and that amidated C-terminal tail is the minimum structure needed to activate KISS1R, also called GPR54. Veracue supplies KP-10 as a lyophilized powder for laboratory research only. It is not intended for human consumption, diagnostic use, or any therapeutic application.

product_description.overview:
Kisspeptin-10 sits at the top of the reproductive endocrine cascade. It binds KISS1R on GnRH neurons in the hypothalamus, which triggers GnRH release, which in turn drives LH and FSH secretion from the anterior pituitary. That upstream position is what makes it a reference compound in neuroendocrine research. Most peptides studied in this space act further down the chain.

Two things about KP-10 are worth stating plainly, because vendor pages routinely blur them.

First, KP-10 is a fragment, not a separate molecule. It is residues 45 to 54 of kisspeptin-54, equivalent to residues 112 to 121 of the KISS1 gene product. Both forms bind the same receptor with comparable affinity. Published Ki values for KP-10 are 1.59 nM at the rat receptor and 2.33 nM at the human receptor.

Second, KP-10 and KP-54 behave very differently in circulation. Plasma half-life for KP-10 is roughly 4 minutes in humans, measured at 3.8 minutes in men and 4.1 minutes in women. KP-54 persists far longer at about 27.6 minutes. Study designs built around one form do not transfer cleanly to the other, and a good deal of the published human fertility work used KP-54 rather than KP-10.
product_description.composition:
Veracue's Kisspeptin-10 is supplied as a lyophilized powder, a single-chain synthetic decapeptide with a C-terminal amide. Lyophilization protects the peptide before reconstitution, which matters here because KP-10 is short, unstructured, and readily attacked by peptidases once it is in solution.

Salt form is part of the product identity, not a footnote. Synthetic KP-10 is typically supplied as an acetate or trifluoroacetate salt, and the counterion affects both net peptide content and how the material behaves in buffer. The counterion for this lot is recorded on the batch COA. [VERIFY: confirm salt form with supplier before publishing]

why_choose_this_product:
The hardest problem with sourcing kisspeptin is not purity. It is knowing what you actually received.

Search for kisspeptin and most listings return a vial labeled simply "Kisspeptin", with no isoform, no sequence, and often no molecular weight. That is a real problem for a peptide family where the two commercial forms differ by 44 residues and by roughly sevenfold in circulating half-life. A researcher who plans around KP-54 pharmacokinetics and receives KP-10 has a failed experiment, not a minor variance.

Veracue lists the isoform in the product name, publishes the full sequence and molecular identifiers on the page, and issues a batch COA carrying both HPLC purity and the measured mass. You can check the mass on the certificate against the expected 1302.45 before the vial leaves the box. That is the standard this listing is built around.

purity_and_quality_standards.body:
Every Kisspeptin-10 lot is tested by an independent laboratory using high-performance liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry, and each lot is issued its own Certificate of Analysis.

The two tests answer different questions, and treating them as interchangeable is one of the more common mistakes in this market.

analytical_methods.establishes: Chromatographic purity as a percentage of total peak area, plus the presence of synthesis byproducts and degradation products
analytical_methods.does_not_establish: Molecular identity. A 99% peak says one species dominates, not which species it is

analytical_methods.establishes: Molecular mass, supporting identity. Distinguishes KP-10 near 1302 Da from KP-54 near 5857 Da without ambiguity
analytical_methods.does_not_establish: Full sequence order. Two peptides with the same composition share a mass

analytical_methods.establishes: Sequence-level confirmation from fragment ion patterns, and detection of truncations or modifications
analytical_methods.does_not_establish: Quantitative purity. It complements HPLC rather than replacing it

analytical_methods.establishes: Salt identity and net peptide content

purity_and_quality_standards.closing:
For Kisspeptin-10 specifically, two things are worth checking on any certificate. Confirm the reported mass sits near 1302 Da rather than near 5857 Da, which separates KP-10 from KP-54 immediately. Then look for oxidation, since the tryptophan at position 3 is the residue most likely to pick up 16 Da.

A purity figure on its own does not establish sterility, biological activity, or suitability for any use in humans. It describes one measurement of one lot.

regulatory_status.body:
There is no FDA-approved kisspeptin drug product in the United States, in any isoform.

Kisspeptin-10 was reviewed by name at the FDA Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee meeting on October 29, 2024, nominated for the treatment of secondary hypogonadism in men. FDA recommended against including it on the 503A Bulks List, and the Committee voted unanimously against inclusion, 0 in favor and 11 opposed, citing a lack of convincing safety and efficacy data. That vote means KP-10 is not available to compounding pharmacies as a bulk drug substance.

faq.question: Which kisspeptin isoform is this product?
faq.answer: This is Kisspeptin-10, the ten-residue fragment, sequence YNWNSFGLRF-NH2, CAS 374675-21-5. It is not Kisspeptin-54. The two are different chemical entities with different molecular weights, different CAS numbers and very different circulating half-lives, so check the isoform on any kisspeptin listing before ordering.

faq.question: What is the difference between Kisspeptin-10 and Kisspeptin-54?
faq.answer: KP-10 is the C-terminal fragment of KP-54, residues 45 to 54. Both activate the same receptor with comparable affinity, because the amidated C-terminal tail they share is the part the receptor recognizes. The practical difference is stability. KP-10 has a plasma half-life near 4 minutes in humans while KP-54 runs close to 28 minutes. Molecular weights are 1302.45 and roughly 5857 respectively, which is why mass spectrometry separates them instantly.

faq.question: Are KISS1, kisspeptin and KISS1R the same thing?
faq.answer: No, and conflating them is a frequent error. KISS1 is the gene that encodes the kisspeptin precursor protein. Kisspeptin is the peptide family produced when that precursor is cleaved, including KP-54, KP-14, KP-13 and KP-10. KISS1R, also called GPR54, is the receptor those peptides bind. A product cannot correctly be called "KISS1 peptide".

faq.question: How does Kisspeptin-10 work?
faq.answer: KP-10 binds KISS1R, a Gq/11-coupled receptor on GnRH neurons. Receptor activation drives phospholipase C, which generates IP3 and DAG, which raise intracellular calcium and activate protein kinase C. That combination depolarizes the neuron and promotes pulsatile GnRH release, which then stimulates LH and FSH secretion from the anterior pituitary. Kisspeptin acts on the hypothalamus, not directly on the pituitary.

faq.question: Does a 99% HPLC result confirm this is Kisspeptin-10 and not another isoform?
faq.answer: No. HPLC measures chromatographic purity, meaning how much of the sample is one dominant species. It does not identify which species that is. Mass confirmation does that job, since KP-10 near 1302 Da and KP-54 near 5857 Da cannot be mistaken for each other by mass. Read the two results together, not separately.

faq.question: What does mass spectrometry confirm, and what does it miss?
faq.answer: It confirms the molecular mass matches the expected value, which strongly supports identity and rules out the wrong isoform. It does not confirm the order of residues, because peptides with identical composition share a mass. Sequence-level confirmation needs MS/MS or peptide mapping, which not every research supplier provides.

faq.question: What should I check on the Certificate of Analysis?
faq.answer: Confirm the lot number matches your vial, since a sample COA from a different batch tells you nothing about the material in hand. Check that the reported mass sits near 1302 Da. Check the HPLC purity figure and the method. Look at the testing date. Check whether a counterion is identified, because that affects net peptide content.

faq.question: Why does the molecular weight on the COA differ from 1302.45?
faq.answer: 1302.45 is the free base. Synthetic peptides are usually supplied as acetate or trifluoroacetate salts, and the counterion adds mass. A certificate reporting net peptide content will also read lower than the gross vial weight. Neither is an error, but the convention should be stated so figures can be compared.

faq.question: Is Kisspeptin FDA approved?
faq.answer: No kisspeptin form has FDA approval for any indication. Kisspeptin-10 was reviewed by the FDA Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee on October 29, 2024, and the Committee voted unanimously, 0 to 11, against adding it to the 503A Bulks List, citing insufficient safety and efficacy data.

faq.question: Has Kisspeptin-10 been studied in humans?
faq.answer: Yes, in physiological research. Intravenous KP-10 produces a dose-dependent rise in LH in healthy volunteers. The important caveat is that most of the well-known human fertility research, including the IVF oocyte maturation trials, used Kisspeptin-54 rather than KP-10. Check which form a paper used before applying it to a KP-10 protocol.

faq.question: Why do most suppliers stock KP-10 rather than KP-54?
faq.answer: Synthesis cost and difficulty. A ten-residue peptide is straightforward to make at high purity. A 54-residue peptide is far harder and considerably more expensive, which is why KP-54 listings are rare and priced accordingly.

faq.question: How should Kisspeptin-10 be stored?
faq.answer: Frozen and protected from light while lyophilized. After reconstitution, refrigerate, aliquot, and use within your protocol's stability window. Minimize freeze-thaw cycles, since KP-10's short unstructured sequence gives it little protection against degradation.
